tone.summary: A warm, singing blues tone built around a classic Marshall-style stack (UK 45) with sustaining overdrive and wah pedal effects.

keep wah and delay as decisive

rig.name: Joe Bonamassa - Sloe Gin (Live) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise inherent in blues-rock playing.
Provide sustaining overdrive and warm grit suitable for blues lead lines.
blocks.gap: The 'Blues OD' might be an alternative, but Green OD offers a more versatile, singing quality needed here.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required wah sweep for classic blues lead tones.
Add subtle harmonic richness and sustain without sounding overly aggressive (used as a secondary gain stage).
blocks.gap: This slot is used to ensure enough gain structure before the amp, complementing Green OD.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-style stack required for blues-rock lead tones.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound matching the Marshall amp model.
Sculpt the tone for maximum singing quality and clarity in the lead voice.
Implement the required short delay repeats for depth and space.
Add natural room ambience to give the lead tone depth without muddying it.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and tonal depth for a more authentic blues-rock lead sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage, singing quality of the Marshall stack.
